readiness.mainReason: No blocking rule fired: the decision is clear, the core recommendation is sourced inline and de-risked with a soft launch, so what remains is refinement.
readiness.highestRiskIssue: The year-one figure on slide 8 shows gross membership income without the cost to run the scheme, so the net contribution is not yet visible.
readiness.whatCouldChangeIt: A confirmed cost side that made the scheme net-negative, or a coordinator capacity limit the input did not state, could demote it to Needs targeted revision.

strengths.point: The deck is answer-first: the recommendation is the title and the decision is restated plainly on slide 2.
strengths.quote: Client E should launch a paid membership scheme, starting with a single tier in the autumn.

strengths.point: Claims are sourced inline, so the argument is traceable.
strengths.quote: Project grants are 80% of Client E's income (2024 accounts) and each is single-year.

strengths.point: The load-bearing assumption is flagged and de-risked with a soft launch before the full commitment.
strengths.quote: A soft launch to the most engaged 200 contacts tests both before the full launch.

strengths.point: The first steps name an owner, a timeline and a go-no-go measure.
strengths.quote: The Client E coordinator owns the launch.

findings.title: The membership case shows gross revenue but not the cost to run the scheme.
findings.principle: Net contribution: a financial case shows the cost to earn the revenue, not only the top line.
findings.diagnosis: Slide 8 gives about 5,000 pounds of year-one income from the 8% conversion. Slides 6 and 7 assert admin is low and the member benefits use existing capacity, but no cost is netted against the 5,000 so the client cannot see the contribution.

evidence.quote: If 8% of the mailing list joins at 45 pounds, that is about 5,000 pounds in year one.

findings.why: A board weighing membership against grant income wants the net it can rely on, not the gross, so the top line alone understates the question it must decide.
findings.reflect: What does it cost Client E to run the two members-only events, the partner discount and the admin, and what is the net after that.
findings.fix: Add a line netting the running cost against the 5,000 pounds so the client sees the contribution rather than the top line. Keep it a directional estimate, not invented precision.

findings.title: The 8% conversion is anchored on an event-attendance rate, a different behavior than paying to join.
findings.principle: Evidence Grounding: benchmark an assumption against behavior of the same kind.
findings.diagnosis: Slide 8 calls the 8% conservative against the 32% attendance rate. Attending an event is a lighter commitment than paying 45 pounds a year, so the 32% is a weak anchor for a paid-conversion rate even though the deck rightly flags 8% as the thing to test.

evidence.quote: The 8% assumption is conservative against the 32% attendance rate and is the main thing to test.

findings.why: The whole year-one number turns on the 8%, so its anchor should be paid-behavior, or explicitly the soft-launch result, rather than free attendance.
findings.reflect: What is the closest paid-conversion benchmark you can find, from the comparable groups or the first cohort, rather than free attendance.
findings.fix: Caveat the 32% anchor and lean the estimate on the soft-launch result or a paid-membership comparator. Directional only.

comments.problem: Titles "What members get" and "Risks and what we are assuming" are topic labels, unlike the answer-first titles elsewhere.
comments.why: The deck is otherwise readable from its titles alone, so two label titles break that skim.
comments.fix: Rewrite them as assertions (the takeaway of the slide) so the titles carry the whole argument.

comments.problem: Slide 8 sets the year-one target at 8% while slide 10 sets the full-launch gate at 5%, and the deck does not say why the gate is lower than the target.
comments.why: Two thresholds that look inconsistent read as an oversight rather than a deliberate lower bar to proceed.
comments.fix: State in one line why the go gate sits below the target so the two numbers read as intentional.

questionsForLead: Did the team confirm the coordinator has capacity to own a launch on top of current duties, given no constraints were provided in the input.
What does running the membership cost across events, partner discount and admin, and is the year-one net still worth it after that.
Is about 5,000 pounds a material dent in the 80% grant concentration, or is the real value the learning from the pilot.

learningNote.lesson: A financial recommendation is judged on the net it delivers, so show the cost to earn the revenue next to the revenue itself.
learningNote.weakHabit: Putting a gross revenue figure in the deck without the cost line that turns it into a contribution.
learningNote.exercise: For any revenue projection, list every cost needed to deliver it and compute the net before the number goes on a slide.

notAssessed: Whether the running cost of the members-only events, the partner discount and the admin nets against the 5,000 pounds. The deck does not quantify it.
Whether the Client E coordinator has capacity to own the launch. Known constraints were not provided in the input.
Whether the 8% conversion assumption holds. It is flagged as the main thing to test and no source was provided.
